newsitem.title: GERMANY: Vereinsbank downgrades Douglas to neutral.
newsitem.headline: Vereinsbank downgrades Douglas to neutral.

text.p: Analysts at Bayerische Vereinsbank on Tuesday said they had downgraded their rating of German speciality retailer Douglas Holding AG to market neutral from buy after a strong share performance in recent months.
In a research note Vereinsbank said shareholders should take profits in the perfume and cosmetics chain after the sharp gains, which have taken the share to a high valuation.

Douglas, part of the MDAX index of mid-capitalisation shares, has rallied from a year-low of 46.50 marks in January to peak at 67.50 marks on October 2. The stock was today down 1.50 marks at 63.10 in late trading on the Frankfurt stock exchange.

Douglas has been a leading performer in a sector hit by stagnant consumer demand where many companies have suffered sharp share price losses. Vereinsbank warned that retail stocks tend to perform badly in the fourth quarter despite the Christmas shopping season.

Vereinsbank expects Douglas' 1996 earnings per share to rise to three marks from 2.80 marks last year, gaining again in 1997 to 3.35 marks. The prospective price-earnings ratio is estimated at 21.5 for 1996 and 19.3 for 1997.
